Subject: GPU pool commit cadence for upcoming deals - weekly sync

Team,

Attached is a proposal for how we should commit dedicated GPUs against the current pipeline for the next 90 days. Highlights: Nimbus pilot (DEAL-8947) and Acme PoC are time-sensitive and will need guaranteed reserved slots if we want to meet their latency SLOs. I pulled forecasted Q2 token run rates from Sales and translated them into sustained GPU-days.

Quick summary:
- Nimbus (pilot) — estimate 8 A100-equivalent GPUs for 6 weeks (burstable to 12) — recommended reserved commit start 2026-03-15.
- Acme (PoC) — 4 GPUs for 8 weeks (steady) — prefer reserved vs burst due to data isolation requirements.
- Zephyr expansion (pilot → prod) — 6 GPUs but flexible (can be handled with burst for 3–4 weeks).

Please review the attached pool_commit_proposal.xlsx and pipeline_forecast_Mar8.pdf for the per-deal math and assumptions. Key asks before EOD Tuesday:
1) Infra: confirm available reserved capacity in us-west/us-east and any hard constraints (Ben).
2) Finance: preliminary pricing / impact on committed-revenue run rate (Kimberly).
3) Sales: confirm deal dates and whether customers require start dates earlier than proposed (Karthik, Laura).

Attachments: [Attachment: pool_commit_proposal.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)], [Attachment: pipeline_forecast_Mar8.pdf (pdf, 220KB)]

Thanks — Marcus

---
Marcus Lin
Head of Demand Planning, Redwood Inference

- Nimbus (DEAL-8947) is aiming for a pilot start on 2026-03-22 (they have an internal demo on the 24th). They will accept a phased commit (4 GPUs Day 1, spike to 8 within the first week) but prefer the reserved SLA by the demo date.

Laura / team — infra update:

- us-west pool has 24 A100-equivalent reserved GPUs free for new commitments today. However, we currently have scheduled node maintenance the week of 2026-03-16 that removes ~6 GPUs from available capacity for two days (planned). We can coordinate maintenance windows but that means any commitment effective 03/15 would need a short-term routing plan.
- us-east has ~10 free reserved GPUs but higher latency to a subset of customer regions—Nimbus prefers us-west.

Recommendation:
1) Prioritize Nimbus for a phased reserved commit in us-west (start with 4 reserved, then add 4 after maintenance completes). Use burst capacity for the interim week.
2) Acme should be reserved in us-east if they accept slightly higher p99; otherwise we should negotiate the contract start date to after the maintenance window.

Also noted: we have an internal policy requiring a minimum 30-day notice for converting burst to reserved. That would affect Zephyr if they want to go reserved quickly.

—Ben
Senior Infra PM, Redwood Inference
